A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ToddlerDiffusion, and their supplied text, equations, tables and figures are readable. However, v1 refers to supplementary COCO results, derivations and implementation details that are absent from its PDF. Those materials cannot be fully matched against v2's included Appendices A–C.

before.justification: V1 reports original LSUN-Churches generation experiments, quantitative comparisons, architecture and augmentation ablations, and qualitative editing results.

after.justification: V2 reports original generation results on LSUN-Churches, CelebA-HQ and ImageNet-100, alongside component ablations, robustness tests and editing comparisons in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The cascaded bridge framework remains, but v2 adds FastSAM segmentation with dominant-color extraction for palettes, moves palette generation from latent to pixel space, and introduces DDPM inversion for real-image editing. Section 3.4 also adapts pretrained SD-v1.5 using residual prediction and full-model fine-tuning. These are substantive component and procedure changes.

E1.justification: V2 adds CelebA-HQ face generation and ImageNet-100 class-conditioned synthesis; v1 used ImageNet for training the Sketch-FID evaluator. V2 also evaluates real-image editing and conflicting-label/perturbed-sketch scenarios. COCO disappears from the reported coverage, although its promised v1 results are unavailable. LAION-Art appears only in v2's abstract, without identifiable experimental support.

E2.justification: V1 Table 4 compares against LDM, U-ViT, DiT, MDT and MaskDIT; v2's generation benchmark retains only LDM. V2 adds evaluated editing/control comparators: SDEdit and ControlNet in Figure 7, SEED-X in Figure 15, and PnP, Pix2Pix-Zero, ControlNet, Uni-ControlNet and GLIGEN in Figure 21. T2I-Adapter is cited but has no displayed comparison row.

E3.justification: The LSUN benchmark changes from v1's two-stage, 50-epoch setup to v2's three-stage framework with 250-epoch results and revised network sizes. Efficiency reporting changes from per-epoch timing on four V100s to 400-epoch training totals on four A100s. New SD-v1.5 comparisons use five-epoch fine-tuning and sketch augmentations. CLIP-FID is removed from the benchmark metrics.

E4.justification: V2 adds bridge-versus-concatenation and prediction-objective ablations, sketch-intensity sensitivity, conflicting-label tests, structured-edge perturbations, and explicit failure examples. V1's architecture-size sweep is removed. The existing cutout/dropout and condition-truncation analyses largely move to Appendix A.6; their relocation is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or statistical error bars. The shading in v2 Figure 4 fills performance gaps between methods, rather than representing uncertainty.

E6.justification: Benchmark results are extensively replaced and expanded. LSUN FID changes from 10.63 versus LDM's 15.16 at 50 epochs in v1 Table 4 to 6.19 versus 7.30 at 250 epochs in v2 Table 1; this is not a same-setting improvement. V2 adds results for other datasets, ablations and editing comparisons. The retained truncation table also changes the best overall FID from 10.6 to 9.5, although v2's accompanying prose still says 10.6.

T1.justification: The conditional ELBO and central reverse mean/variance expressions remain. V2 adds the formal Schrödinger-bridge KL minimization problem, endpoint constraints, an SDE and a residual-prediction identity. Appendix A.1 supplies a worked reverse-process derivation that v1 only refers to in its unavailable supplement; its novelty relative to that supplement cannot be established.

C1.justification: V2 expands the central capability claims to consistent editing of real images and explicitly claims a unified combination of control, interactivity and efficiency. It removes v1's explicit claim of surpassing all efficient diffusion methods. The headline efficiency claim changes from three times faster with a 3.76-times smaller architecture to twice as fast with a three-times smaller architecture; the ten-step training claim remains.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations for prediction-objective behavior, data-dependent sketch intensity, and geometry/style preservation under conflicting conditions. It also discusses limitations from poor sketches, unsuccessful generations, insufficient convergence of five-epoch comparison methods, and the difficulty of adapting pretrained SD weights. The earlier interpretation of inter-stage error accumulation is retained in Appendix A.6.

D1.justification: V1's general optimizer, initialization, learning-rate and training-batch disclosures, plus detailed channel/residual-block configurations, are omitted. V2 adds per-stage resource measurements, hardware details, the full-model SD fine-tuning recipe with a suggested 1e-6 learning rate, and segmentation-based palette instructions. A project-website pointer replaces the supplementary-code/future-release statement; actual resource availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 substantially shifts positioning toward hierarchical generation, spatial conditioning and editing. It introduces relationships to Composer, FineGAN, PartGAN, ControlNet-related methods, DDPM inversion and SEED-X, while dropping references associated with several efficient-generation baselines. Schrödinger bridges were already central and cited in v1, rather than being a newly introduced research connection.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten. V1's standalone diffusion-preliminaries/limitations section disappears, and the method is reorganized around conditional/unconditional modules, guidance and consistency. Algorithms and several stage-specific analyses move to appendices, substantially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: V2 switches from two-column to single-column layout, replaces the overview with a capabilities montage, adds a trajectory diagram, restructures benchmark tables and redraws performance plots. Editing and robustness grids expand substantially. Existing architecture diagrams, algorithms and fusion tables are relocated or reformatted, with some earlier editing examples reused.

improvement.justification: V2 makes generalization and design choices more assessable through actual CelebA-HQ/ImageNet-100 results, direct bridge/objective ablations, and robustness and failure examples. These strengthen evidence beyond v1's predominantly LSUN-based presentation. The gains are tempered by removal of broader generation baselines and important training details, plus unresolved inconsistencies between revised displays and prose, notably Figure 13 and Table 6. The supplied PDFs therefore support a positive but limited net improvement, rather than an unqualified substantial quality gain.
